title: SQLite Critical CVEs or LLM Slop?
titleZh: SQLite 关键 CVE 还是 LLM Slop？
author: ymir_e
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Over the past few days, a newly created GitHub repo (programmervuln/cveadvisory-) published a batch of SQLite vulnerability advisories (as part of other 50+ CVEs which we believe are also LLM slop except from one). NVD quickly flagged these as critical, and CISA's ADP agreed. But when JFrog security researchers dug in to verify, the claims fell apart:

The cited code didn't even exist in those versions or referenced unrelated logic. When testing the PoC payloads they didn’t work (not triggering any crash). None of these CVEs are listed on SQLite’s official advisory page (which is a gold standard for tracking actual vulnerabilities). All advisories in this repo seem AI generated when testing them with Gptzero

Combining all advisories into one file triggers AI-generated content warnings This made us question the reliability of these CVEs as well as understanding that these CVEs may be LLM slop. While investigating one of the CVEs yesterday, CVE-2026-51302, we saw that Red Hat initially assigned it a 10.0 Critical severity score:
Looking at the CVE again today, we noticed that the score has since been downgraded to 7.6 High.
CVE Reported Flaw CVSS NVD Metadata Audit Finding

comments.author: gortok
comments.textRawHtml:
We can chalk this up as another example of over-exhuberance by what folks believe LLMs can accomplish vs. what they actually are.

LLM-based “AI” is able to use its vast corpus of inputs and calculate the most statistically likely output in a given situation. It is probabilistic, and when you are dealing with probabilities in a situation where certainties, not probabilities, matter, you’re going to get dinged on credibility massively when your LLM-based “AI” gets the probabilities wrong at best, or in this case, claims a line of code generates a vulnerability when it is, in fact, a code comment.

LLMs are text-prediction engines. They are not Artificial Intelligence, and shouldn’t not be treated in any form or fashion as if they possess intelligence. What bothers me about this entire situation is that presumably the folks that relied on the LLM-based “AI” to generate these vulnerabilities knew (or should have known) enough about their tool to know this would happen, but did not.

Now, we all pay the consequence, to the tune of hundreds of thousands if not millions of dollars of wasted productivity from teams that have to deal with the resulting fall-out of this usage of “AI”.

A human must verify everything an LLM presents as fact. Everything. If you don’t, we all pay the price. LLMs do not remove the onus of responsibility on the human being, if anything they amplify it because LLMs can generate lots more output more quickly that needs to be verified than humans can.
comments.textZhHtml:
我们可以将此视为过度兴奋的另一个例子，即人们认为 LLM 可以完成的任务与他们实际完成的任务之间的差距。

基于 LLM 的“人工智能”能够使用其庞大的输入语料库，并计算出在给定情况下最有统计可能性的输出。 它是概率性的，当你在确定性而不是概率更重要的情况下处理概率时，当你的基于法学硕士的“人工智能”得到的概率最多是错误的，或者在这种情况下，声称一行代码实际上是代码注释时会产生漏洞，那么你的可信度就会受到严重损害。

法学硕士是文本预测引擎。 它们不是人工智能，不应该以任何形式或方式被视为拥有智能。 这整个情况让我困扰的是，想必依赖基于 LLM 的“AI”来生成这些漏洞的人们对他们的工具足够了解（或应该了解），知道这种情况会发生，但他们没有。

现在，我们都付出了后果，数十万甚至数百万美元的生产力浪费，来自团队必须处理这种使用“AI”所带来的后果。

人类必须验证 LLM 所呈现的所有内容。事实。一切。如果你不这样做，我们都会付出代价。 法学硕士并没有消除人类的责任，甚至放大了责任，因为法学硕士可以比人类更快地产生更多需要验证的输出。

children.author: elmer2
children.textRawHtml:
Many people with no skills are taking advantage of the LLM craze to artificially inflate their own value. I see it every day on LinkedIn.

People that previously have barely any experience in tech, now being hired in AI startups because they are good bullshitters.
children.textZhHtml:
许多没有技能的人正在利用LLM热潮人为地抬高自己的价值。我每天都会在 LinkedIn 上看到这种情况。

以前几乎没有任何技术经验的人现在被人工智能初创公司聘用，因为他们很会胡说八道。

children.author: prh8
children.textRawHtml: Countless directors and managers are now cosplaying as engineers. I've seen so many myself and that's just my tiny slice of this engineering world

children.textRawHtml: It is pretty funny to see the shoe on the other foot, since it's usually software engineers with unearned arrogance about other fields.

children.textRawHtml: What fields do you see devs think they know about? I’ve never personally seen this with other devs I work with but obviously small sample size…

children.author: afavour
children.textRawHtml:
In my experience, product. There’s a pervasive view that product is easy, that anyone working in it is a dunderhead who gets in the way of engineers doing the really worthwhile work. In reality, it would just mean they rewrite the software five times and have zero customers.

Oh, design too. I’ve met many engineers who simply don’t see any value in design.
children.textZhHtml:
根据我的经验，产品。人们普遍认为产品很简单，任何从事产品工作的人都是笨蛋，会妨碍工程师做真正有价值的工作。事实上，这仅仅意味着他们重写了软件五次并且客户为零。

哦，设计也是如此。我遇到过很多工程师，他们根本看不到设计的任何价值。

children.author: ekholm_e
children.textRawHtml: This. I'm a former teacher. I left to get a PhD in educational psychology, and now I'm a data scientist for a large school division. The number of ed tech companies I interact with who clearly have little grasp of research-based best practices in education is staggering. But they can all build slick-looking websites and dashboards.
children.textZhHtml: 这个。我以前是一名老师。我离开是为了获得教育心理学博士学位，现在我是一个大学校部门的数据科学家。我接触过的教育科技公司数量惊人，他们显然对基于研究的最佳教育实践知之甚少。但他们都可以构建外观漂亮的网站和仪表板。

children.author: luke5441
children.textRawHtml:
I don't think it is much of a problem that dabblers get into Internet arguments about things they are not experts in. After all the easiest way to get a correct answer/learn something is to say something wrong.

Of course this should be differentiated from a professional setting.

And under no circumstances should we put that stuff into the knowledge bases we base our "AI" on without making sure it takes into account the context.
children.textZhHtml:
我认为，涉足者在互联网上争论他们不擅长的事情并不是什么大问题。毕竟，获得正确答案/学习某些东西的最简单方法就是说一些错误的东西。

当然，这应该与专业环境区分开来。

并且在任何情况下，我们都不应该将这些东西放入我们作为“AI”基础的知识库中，而不确保它考虑到了上下文。

children.textRawHtml: There have always been people with no tech experience building startups generating spaghetti code. It's just that now it looks a lot more polished.
children.textZhHtml: 总有一些没有技术经验的人创建初创公司并生成意大利面条式代码。只是现在看起来更加精致了。

children.author: Jensson
children.textRawHtml:
> It's just that now it looks a lot more polished.

Yes, and that is the problem. It used to be if a product looked polished it was fairly polished engineering wise as well if we compare to todays AI slop. You can see that on steam, before AI slop games a game that looked polished mostly worked. But today you can get a game that looks like they put in a lot of effort, but its all AI slop and everything is flaky and broken, I've had way more such experiences the last few months than before that.

A human coder that was capable of coding a complex game typically also was good enough and tested things to make most things work. There were bugs etc, but at least buttons did things.
children.textZhHtml:
> 只是现在看起来更加精致了。

是的，这就是问题所在。过去，如果一个产品看起来很精致，那么如果我们与今天的人工智能相比，它在工程方面也相当精致。你可以看到，在steam上，在AI游戏出现之前，看起来很精致的游戏基本上都能运行。但今天你可以得到一款看起来他们付出了很多努力的游戏，但它全是人工智能，一切都是片状和破碎的，在过去的几个月里，我比以前有更多这样的经历。

能够编写复杂游戏的人类编码员通常也足够好，并测试了一些东西以使大多数东西都能工作。虽然存在错误等，但至少按钮可以发挥作用。

children.textRawHtml: Engineers cosplay as physicists and mathematicians every day. What's your point? Think of it pragmatically. If they can do the job they can do the role.
children.textZhHtml: 工程师每天都扮演物理学家和数学家。你的观点是什么？务实地思考一下。如果他们能胜任这份工作，他们就能胜任这个角色。

children.author: ruszki
children.textRawHtml:
> If they can do the job they can do the role.

Obviously.

Can they do the job? Because right now, government decisions are based on AI generated code, which was verified by nobody who can do that. So the cost of an unsatisfactory answer is quite high.
children.textZhHtml:
> 如果他们能胜任这项工作，他们就能胜任这个角色。

显然。

他们能胜任这项工作吗？因为现在，政府决策是基于人工智能生成的代码，而没有人能够验证这些代码。因此，一个不令人满意的答案的成本是相当高的。
